whoRunsThis.alsoRuns: The operator also runs automated trading systems (memecoin trading bots) on other hosts, with their own wallets. Those systems are not part of this platform and their code is private.
whoRunsThis.refusal: Every one of those systems refuses to buy any coin launched through this platform, by mint address and by ticker, on every chain they trade. The refusal is code, not a promise: src/lib/ownTokens.ts reads config/own-tokens.json and every entry path asks it before a buy. A list that cannot be read refuses every entry (fail closed). Both files are in the public repository.

bounty.fundedFrom: the developer fee (25 bps of curve volume)

wallets.label: operations wallet
wallets.description: Pays the keeper's transaction fees and rent, and the hosting. Holds no platform coin. Funded by the operator and by the developer fee.

wallets.label: program deployer
wallets.description: The key that deploys burn_receipts. Its upgrade authority is handed to the Squads vault at launch and set to none after the audit; the deployer key itself then holds nothing.

wallets.label: keeper data key
wallets.description: The keeper signs readings and cranks; LaunchLab's recorded creator is the program's fee PDA. As an attester (quorum 1 at launch) it signs settled readings; as fee payer it sends cranks, claims and health checks. It cannot change a rule, burn more than the rule says, or withdraw from any fee PDA (see the Powers Register).

wallets.label: developer fee wallet
wallets.description: Receives the platform's 25 bps of curve volume (PlatformConfig.platformClaimFeeWallet). Its full ledger is read from chain on this page.

wallets.label: LaunchLab platform admin
wallets.description: May change the platform fee bps, the claim wallet, cpConfigId, platformCpCreator and the LP split for launches not yet migrated. Holder: a dedicated encrypted key held by the operator; it cannot be transferred to the Squads vault (Raydium derives the platform id from the admin key) — disclosed as an untimelocked power (Powers Register, 'Powers outside the program'). Any change shows on this page within one cycle; initialize_token pins cpConfigId, platformCpCreator and the LP scales, and the launch gate re-reads them immediately before each create.

wallets.label: Squads 2-of-3 vault
wallets.description: Holds the program upgrade authority (48 h time lock), the platform authority (may only RAISE the pre-audit burn-pool cap, 48 h timelock) and each token's config authority (attester set only, 48 h timelock).

wallets.label: Squads member — owner, hardware key
wallets.description: One of the three signers of the vault.

wallets.label: Squads member — owner, second key
wallets.description: One of the three signers of the vault.

wallets.label: Squads member — trusted third party
wallets.description: One of the three signers of the vault; named here when the owner has their consent.

wallets.label: $DEFICIT mint keypair (public key)

rehearsals.text: $REHEARSAL — a throwaway coin created under the real platform config on <date> to prove fee routing and burns on mainnet; LP burned; not for trading. Its mint and the date go here when it happens; until then: not done.

limitations.text: Quorum 1 at launch: the operator's keeper key is the only attester. The program verifies signatures and the quorum, not the reading itself. A second, independent attester is required before strangers launch.

Switchboard Technology Labs ended all oracle services on 2026-09-25. The Switchboard attester in this code is built against the pinned SDK and cannot run live. The planned replacements — a Reclaim zkTLS proof of the source response posted by a relayer key, and/or a second human operator running the reader on another machine — are not live. The 'attester #2 within 14 days' line on this page is the schedule, not a built thing.

Kalshi is read off-chain: the keeper reads settled results from Kalshi's public API and signs them. Nothing on chain verifies that reading beyond the attester signatures. The series' settlement source URL is in every receipt so anyone can recompute. Kalshi's API terms on redistribution have not been reviewed.
One-shot markets are allowed: a coin bound to a single market resolves once, on that market's close, and its supply is fixed after that. The token page says so.

Pre-audit cap: each burn pool spends from at most 25 SOL per burn day; SOL above the cap stays in the fee PDA until the next day. In the program it is PlatformConfig's cap with a sunset of at most 365 days, raisable only through a 48 h public timelock; the keeper models the same cap. Until the program is deployed only the keeper enforces it.
No devnet rehearsal has run yet. It is scheduled for the first weekday morning after the program merges: three tokens, cranks from a second machine, the create wizard end to end.

The burn_receipts program is not deployed on any public cluster. The app runs on FakeBurnProgram and FakeLaunchLab; every page and route says so; the launch wizard refuses mainnet and returns ready: false.

Raydium LaunchLab's PlatformConfig admin has no on-chain timelock (LaunchLab has none) and cannot be moved to the Squads vault after creation (the platform id is derived from the admin key). It is a dedicated encrypted key held by the operator, disclosed as an untimelocked power; the mitigations are the pins taken at initialize_token, the pre-create re-check and the live-vs-designed comparison on this page, not a lock.
The operator's contact address is a TODO constant (OPERATOR_CONTACT_TODO). It is filled in before launch.
deploy/ has a unit for the $DEFICIT keeper only; the multi-token Burnticker keeper and the hourly audit timer have no systemd units yet.

The live platform config, the fee ledger and wallet holdings on this page are read from an RPC. Without BURNTICKER_RPC_URL on the host the page says the live reads are unavailable instead of showing stale numbers.

The public repository has not been created yet. The carve-out script and the allowlist exist in the private monorepo (scripts/ops/publish-public-repo.sh, config/public-repo.allowlist); the owner creates the organisation and repository and runs it.

policies.text: On X: nothing is deleted. A mistake is corrected in-thread, with the receipt (the transaction and the recomputation) attached.
No Telegram or Discord: Burnticker and $DEFICIT communicate only through @burnticker / @USA_DEFICIT on X and the public repository. Any channel claiming otherwise is not ours.
Failure definition: if any coin on this platform trades at any price, nothing changes — no relaunch, no v2, no rebrand, no change to a rule. The rule runs and the receipts post.
No paid promotion, no influencer payments, no referral kickbacks. No price talk and no countdowns.
The platform never buys any coin, including its own. Burn pools buy only inside crank_buyback, by the rule, and burn what they receive. The operator's trading bots refuse platform coins.
Nothing on any surface is described as coming later. If it is not built, this page lists it as not built, with its status.
Creators receive no cash from fees; the creator-fee slot pays the burn pool, 100%. Zero team allocation on any coin. Seed deposits to a burn pool are gifts with no claim.
The platform does not reply to or amplify return-marketing. A creator who markets returns using our pages loses the embed, not the rule.
Rules, readings and receipts are append-only. Corrections are new entries that name what they correct; the incident log and this decision log are never edited after the fact.
The memecoin disclaimer and the event-contract disclosure sit on every surface that describes the mechanic.
